text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.6% today to $142.28, continuing a four-day rally that's recovered most of last week's losses. The stock has climbed nearly $6 in five trading days as crude oil prices stabilized around $89–$92 per barrel; energy stocks often track oil prices closely since higher crude supports earnings from production and refining. The rally appears tied to modest oil price stability after the recent weakness, rather than a specific company announcement.

The broader context matters here: heating oil prices are up 59% year-over-year, which typically signals strong demand from refiners and support for crude prices heading into winter. However, the IEA also reported that Russian crude production is recovering and global oil supply has moved back into surplus, which could put downward pressure on prices longer term—a headwind that may explain why the stock is still down 7.6% over two weeks despite today's gain.
